phrase.text: Limits are resources set by whoever runs the program —depth, statements, memory, time— and are not part of the language: a program that does not reach them gives the same result under any configuration.

runs.text: Limits are resources set by whoever runs the program —depth, statements, memory, time— and are not part of the language: a program that does not reach them gives the same result under any configuration.

caption.text: Four resources with their cap. Exhausting depth or cells is a program failure; exhausting statements or time is a limit cut.

blocks.title: A recursion that exhausts depth

entries.text: Every host allows at least 1000 frames and 4194304 cells.
The app uses 1000 frames; the terminal, 100000 and no statement budget.
No limit exhausts the host's stack or produces an internal failure.
Network and JSON limits do not end the program: they arrive as error values.

points.text: Limits are configured by the host; they are not part of the language.
They are measured in deterministic units.
Depth and cells fail; statements and time cut.
